page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 core-to-memory general-purpose ratio at 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The architecture operates on x86_64 and supports instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES-NI, and BMI2.

Hardware accelerators are absent, with 0 GPUs available on the instance. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage must be provisioned via remote block storage services. Networking capabilities are anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.u1-c1m4.4xlarge predominantly within mid-tier performance brackets across both single-threaded and multi-threaded evaluations. The instance recorded a single-core Geekbench score of 1396.0 and a multi-core score of 8674.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 19110.27. Memory subsystem performance reached 82.77 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 56.23 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 15.3 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.5 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Machine learning inference runs show typical throughput for smaller parameter models, but larger architectures like 7B models experience constrained prompt processing speeds falling into the bottom quartile.

Resource allocation delivers a balanced profile suited for medium enterprise workloads that do not demand extreme single-thread frequencies or local NVMe input/output operations. The instance is suited for backend web servers, container orchestration nodes, middle-tier enterprise applications, and in-memory caching layers such as Redis.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance offering a balanced configuration of 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon processor at 2.5 GHz and 64.0 GB of memory. Based on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, the instance operates under the KVM hypervisor. It features no integrated local storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring external network block storage for persistence. Network baseline performance is rated at 5 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks across CPU, memory bandwidth, and caching operations exhibit mid-tier, balanced results, highlighted by 15.3 million Redis SET operations per second and steady multi-threaded compilation performance. However, prompt processing for 7B parameter language models lands in the lower performance quartile. The server is well suited for web serving fleets, enterprise microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and memory-backed key-value datastores.
